resolvedQuestions.text: Q1: gate contract + four proven auto-on paths
resolvedQuestions.resolution: answered: FEATURES holds four entries; featureReady = switch-first then one bounded auth probe; four live paths share gate-first fail-open shape; no gate change needed for candidates

resolvedQuestions.text: Q2: spec-track narrowing proof, power, hardening, integration, tests
resolvedQuestions.resolution: answered: repeat inconclusive (stop margin, CI spans zero); 80% power needs 217 decided pairs (~431 rows); relative-only rule needs floors; advisory Gate 1 shape; R1 binds

resolvedQuestions.text: Q3: clarify default proof, power, seam, integration, tests
resolvedQuestions.resolution: answered: 3 of 365 census; 42 of 54 rows refused; power wall (69 discordant at 0.65); seam drops alternatives; shadow logging is the next step

resolvedQuestions.text: Q4: alignment suggestion proof, hardening, integration, tests
resolvedQuestions.resolution: answered: distractor control kills (W=0 L=30, state-anchored pick); fixture corpus cannot prove; masked-state ablation gates the decision

resolvedQuestions.text: Q5: unified proof-or-retire standard, hardening and test plan, ranked next step per feature
resolvedQuestions.resolution: answered: seven-requirement standard; shared-kit amendment set; shadow->canary->live order; ranked next step per feature

keyFindings.title: **P0 — Measure real eligible volume and collect shadow labels before paying for more model rows.** Feature 020's committed-corpus spec records 2 mode-alternative clarifications in 359 prompts and zero gold-in-alternatives. A later read-only census reports 3 total clarifications in 365 prompts: 2 mode clarifications plus 1 checklist clarification; the denominator changed and the 3rd item is not a mode suggestion. Both say the real-use rate remains unmeasured without transcripts. At 2 eligible mode clarifications per 365 prompts, exact 80%-power estimates require 69 discordant pairs at a 0.65 win rate (about 32,000 committed prompts at the fixture's discordance rate), making shadow collection with user picks as labels the practical next step. Confirmation: count actual `action: clarify` events by hub from consented, redacted session metadata, record accepted/overridden picks as labels, and publish counts before another Jev run. keyFindings.title: **P0 — Pre-register an external-validity and power gate before another model run.** Use a consented, redacted, time-separated sample of actual Gate 1 queries, with independent label provenance, `none`/cross-track cases, and enough observations per track to estimate both traffic-weighted utility and worst-track recall. keyFindings.title: **P1 — Apply a common proof-or-retire gate before any feature advances: real, time-separated usage; independent labels; a predeclared strongest-safe baseline; adequate power; absolute and class-specific floors; and passing negative controls.** A `keep` from an authored or proxy fixture cannot answer external validity. A `stop` for too few eligible rows, margin, coverage, or missing labels is unresolved evidence, not a kill; a feature-specific `kill` on a valid prespecified control can close the tested question or backend. keyFindings.label: The gate registers exactly four features (cite-drift, injection-screen, verdict-fallback, hallucination-grader); the three candidates have no FEATURES entry, no JEV_FEATURE_ name and no live call site. Earning a live path means adding a FEATURES entry, a live call site that asks featureReady first, and docs; the gate itself needs no change.

The gate contract is switch-first then one bounded readiness probe: featureSwitch resolves master JEV_FEATURES, the feature env, then aliases (env wins per key over the hook-flags file; only 0/false/no/off switch off); jevReady walks PATH in-process then runs one bounded jev auth status --provider call (10s timeout, output discarded); featureReady composes them. A disabled feature never spawns, proven by the stub-CLI test asserting an empty log.

The four proven live paths share one integration shape: gate first, fail open to the pre-Jev behavior, never block. cite-drift gates runAdvise with featureSwitch plus a version-pinned private adviseGate; injection-screen returns done() when not ready; verdict-fallback resolves auto to jev or noop and records the gate reason; hallucination-grader resolves auto on the 5dim path only and hard-fails an explicit --grader jev without readiness.

The 017 keep did not repeat: the 270-row repeat printed stop (margin) K=270 M=270 A=106 B=82 W=80 L=56 F=48 p=0.02409 with bootstrap accuracy_delta_95_ci=[-0.1185,0.2760] clusters=16; the margin gate needed 27 rows and the gain was 24, while the sign test passed. The baseline rose 68/256 to 82/270 and Jev 97/256 to 106/270. The repeat is inconclusive, not a kill.

Exact binomial power against the margin gate: at the repeat's observed decided-pair win rate 0.588 (80 of 136), 80% power needs 217 decided pairs (~431 rows at the current 50.4% decided rate); at the current 136 decided pairs the MDE is 0.634 (~37 rows / 13.7pp); the repeat as run had 0.399 power at its own effect. A pre-registered power line (n, alpha, MDE) belongs in the report before a third run is read as decisive.
sources: computed: exact binomial tail sum P(2W-n_d>=27), W~Bin(n_d,0.588)

keyFindings.label: The frozen keep rule is relative-only (coverage 10*M>=9*K, margin 10*(A-B)>=M, sign test p<0.05, flips 10*F<=3*M) with no absolute accuracy floor and no per-track floor; A=106/270 (39.3%) would keep if the margin passed. Proving a live win needs operator-set absolute and per-track recall floors.

Today's read-only census (zero model calls) gives 3 clarifications in 365 committed prompts: clarify_mode=2 plus clarify_checklist=1, all in canary sources; the served surface is 2 mode clarifications in 365 (0.55%). The topic's 3-of-359 holds in substance with the denominator moved. The census ends real clarify rate: not measured because --transcripts was not run.

keyFindings.label: The replay refusal is live: --score on the 54-row fixture printed 42 replay-refused (route) rows, then rows: 54 labeled=12 operator=12 committed_gold=0, then stop: fewer than 30 labeled rows (12 labeled), exit 0. The refusal runs before any model call and matches the 049 record (12 of 54 at HEAD). The fixture keep is historical; the current build cannot reach the keep rule.

The power wall: one-sided sign-test 80% power needs 158 discordant pairs at a 0.60 win rate, 69 at 0.65, 37 at 0.70; the fixture held 21. At the fixture's 21/54 discordant rate, 69 pairs need ~177 clarify rows, i.e. ~32,000 committed prompts at today's 2-per-365 mode rate. The keep rule compares against the first alternative while always-none scores 34/54 against Jev's 28; the strongest simple policy is printed but not required to be beaten. A live-win proof needs shadow-collected real rows plus class floors and a strongest-policy bar.
sources: command: exact binomial sign-test power from fixture counts (W=17 L=4 of 54)

keyFindings.label: The distractor-state control kills the verdict: with each row's state rotated to the next row's, the recorded run prints verdict jev: kill K=40 M=40 A=0 B=30 W=0 L=30 F=0 p=0.0000 and W+L=30 interval95=[0.000,0.114]; all 30 discordant rows are losses where the model picked the folder named in the rotated state. The judgment is state-anchored, not content-anchored — a P0 robustness failure of the question shape.

The keep survives only with path-resolved descriptions and the original state: re-measure keep K=40 M=40 A=39 B=30 W=10 L=1 F=0 p=0.0059 baseline=top (311 calls, 102 s), recall 40/40, baseline target=0 top=30 comparator=auto. The ten wins are rows whose label is neither target nor top — real recoveries the distractor control then invalidates as a live predictor.

The corpus is a fixture by construction (target wrong 0/40; labels one arbiter read; comparator=auto chosen on the scored labels) and 11 discordant rows cannot prove a live win (80% power needs 69 at a 0.65 win rate). Proving needs real low-match saves with final destination and label provenance, a pre-declared comparator, a holdout, and either >=69 discordant pairs or an explicit screen-only acceptance.
sources: computed: sign-test power (iteration 3 script, same rule family)

keyFindings.label: The unified proof-or-retire standard has seven requirements (real-traffic corpus + pinned digests; independent labels with provenance; keep rule with absolute and class floors plus a strongest-policy bar; pre-registered power; negative controls pass; fail-open live shape; tests). None of the three features meets all seven today; retirement with evidence is a legitimate terminal state.

The keep-rule family diverges: clarify and alignment carry the kill branch (kill P(X>=L)<=0.05) while track narrowing does not (a significant loss only fails its sign test); no rule has an absolute floor, a per-track/class floor, or requires beating the strongest simple policy. The shared scorer-report.mjs kit is the right amendment site: one kit change plus three rule lines reaches all three scorers.

Ranked next step per feature. Track narrowing (P0): pre-register power + floors, build the real Gate 1 holdout (~217 decided pairs / ~431 rows at the current decided rate), then a third run under the amended rule; R1 binds. Clarify default (P0): run --transcripts to measure the real rate, shadow-log with user picks as labels, require strongest-policy bar and class floors, and extend the routing contract before any suggestion. Alignment (P1): mask folder names from the state and rerun the distractor control; retire the question if it still kills, else rebuild the corpus from real saves.

The auto-on resolution records provenance: auto resolves once before any work to jev only when the gate is ready, otherwise noop, and the resolved grader plus gate reason are recorded so a shifted score is attributable; --grader noop restores the old score.

The test pattern for a gated feature is a stub-CLI fixture: a temp jev script recording argv, injected env/config, the full switch matrix (unset, master, feature, alias, config fallback, env-over-config), readiness pass/fail/no-CLI, a disabled-feature no-spawn proof, frozen FEATURES, and CommonJS reach with zero warnings. New feature tests can reuse this fixture shape and should target the candidate's own question constants, record shape and fallback behavior.

Probability-aware aggregation did not repeat its 017 gain: on the repeat it scored A=102 vs the modal 106 (decided-subset 102/203=0.5025, margin slack -7.0 rows, p=0.05018); the one-call arm scored 103. The three-order protocol buys stability, not accuracy, and the free-row claim is corpus-dependent; the shortlist arm remains unmeasured.

The 049 trust upgrades landed and show in the repeat record: rowSetSha256 + per-row questionSha256 + optionSetSha256 and the model tuple {jev 0.6.2, official, jev-1.13.0} are pinned; --out reuse is refused; --replay scores exactly the recorded rows and reports drops; the cluster bootstrap (16 clusters, 1000 replicates) runs in-report. The remaining trust gap is labels and population, not instrumentation.

Transfer warning persists and clusters are heterogeneous: paraphrase probes favor ripgrep 9/14 to Jev 2/14; per-track accuracy ranges from sk-git 14/19 to sk-design 3/20 (16 of 20 abstained); total abstained=55 (20.4%), with three tracks holding 31 of them. Any live path must be miss-only with fail-open, and sk-design-like clusters need description diagnosis first.

The 049 trust upgrades landed: report.json records rows/labels/options/scorer digests and build identity; class and hub results print with first/second/always-none/strongest baselines; label approver and decision reference are accepted; the early stop (two agreeing orders, third only on disagreement) matched all 54 recorded modal picks in 118 calls against 163. Tests grew 22 to 31.

The seam is confirmed dropped: the engine decision carries decision.clarify.alternatives (the scorer and census read it directly), but the normalized runtime route returns only {hubId, action, selectionKind, targets, effectivePolicyHash, generation} with targets empty on clarify, and resolveRoute serves only that identity-bound shape. A served suggestion needs a routing-owner contract extension first; gold_in_alternatives=0 in every census cell shows the alternatives rarely even contain the gold.

f022-001 still loses with both options described: Jev picks 007-classifier-deep-research at 0.48, 0.58 and 0.43 against the label 001-deep-research. The path-resolved describer fix removed the undescribed-option defect but did not convert the one loss; the row should be adjudicated, not chased.

The trust upgrades landed: kill branch (kill P(X>=L)<=0.05), W+L Wilson interval, discordant rows, corpus/report/scorer pins, label-swap control (W+L=10 [0.722,1.000]; wins sit on rows whose label is neither target nor top), distractor-state arm, and a confidence-gated arm keeping the same verdict at 70 choice calls vs 120. Tests grew 35 to 43.

Ranked next step: build the same 40-row arm with folder names masked out of the state (or an explicit instruction to ignore state folder names) and rerun the distractor-state control; if the kill persists, retire the current question shape with that evidence; if it survives, the feature earns a real-save corpus. One arm run plus a small scorer change gates everything else.

The shared kit is the reuse path: all three scorers import scorer-report.mjs (pins, margin slack, decided subset, cluster bootstrap, intervals, out-dir guard); alignment added the newest controls (label-swap, distractor-state) and the kill branch, clarify the replay refusal and early stop, track narrowing the cluster bootstrap and per-track tables. Port the alignment controls to track narrowing and keep clarify's replay refusal as its strong control.

Integration order is shadow then canary then live behind the unchanged gate: add FEATURES entries (track-narrowing, clarify-default, alignment-suggestion with JEV_FEATURE_* names), a call site asking featureReady first, fail-open fallbacks and provenance recording; precedents are cite-drift (advisory + version-pinned gate), injection-screen (advisory hook, always exits 0) and the two auto graders. Per-feature blockers before any call site: track (corpus + floors), clarify (seam + base rate), alignment (state-anchoring).

cite-drift diverges from the shared readiness check: it uses featureSwitch plus its own adviseGate that additionally requires an exact jev --version match; jevReady has no version pin. Two live-path shapes exist (shared readiness for injection-screen and both graders; version-pinned private readiness for cite-drift), and a version-sensitive candidate can follow the cite-drift precedent.

Cost is latency: p50 325 ms and p95 389 ms per call over 852 planned calls per arm, ~953,885 estimated input tokens (mostly the 17-option block); the one-call arm is within 3 rows of the modal arm (103 vs 106). A live path should serve one call on ambiguous/miss rows only inside a few-hundred-ms budget, keeping three orders offline.

Integration shape: add 'track-narrowing' with env JEV_FEATURE_TRACK_NARROWING to FEATURES and a Gate 1 advisory call site at lookup-trigger-index.mjs:132 that asks featureReady only when the lexical lookup misses or ties, prints an advisory, and fails open to broad search (the cite-drift advisory shape). Prior R1 (keep hard narrowing offline until a real-request holdout passes) is unchanged and strengthened by the repeat.

Integration shape: add 'clarify-default' with env JEV_FEATURE_CLARIFY_DEFAULT to FEATURES and an advisory call site beside action: clarify that suggests one alternative, never replaces the clarification, and fails open on none_of_these, timeout, error, missing credentials or a generation mismatch. Prerequisites: a named reader and scope amendment, shadow logging first (T1), and a payload decision.

Tests to cover beyond the landed refusal/replay/digest/early-stop cases: a shadow-log capture test (user pick as label), a normalized-route alternatives contract test, class-floor assertions (named-mode accuracy plus abstention precision/recall), a strongest-policy-bar verdict case, and a --transcripts end-to-end clarify-rate test (the path exists but was never run).

Integration shape: add 'alignment-suggestion' with env JEV_FEATURE_ALIGNMENT_SUGGESTION to FEATURES and an interactive, flag-gated save-flow suggestion that asks featureReady first, shows one folder with a reason, and lets the existing selection step authorize any switch; never override the below-20% hard block; CLI-explicit saves keep their folder; consent + timeout + kill switch; a 047 D6 amendment is required.

Tests to cover beyond the landed 43 cases: a masked-state variant test (state with folder names removed), a real-save corpus validation fixture with final destinations, label-provenance assertions, an f022-001 adjudication record, and interactive-flow integration tests with a stub jev (fail-open, timeout, consent). The masked-state ablation is the highest-value new test because it probes the distractor failure directly.

Cross-feature test plan: the stub-CLI fixture plus recorded-run replays are the shared pattern; add track narrowing absolute/per-track floor and paraphrase-threshold cases; clarify shadow-capture, normalized-route alternatives contract, strongest-policy-bar and transcripts rate tests; alignment masked-state ablation, real-save corpus validation, label-provenance and interactive fail-open/timeout/consent tests. All offline.

Base rates cap the value: clarify serves 2 mode clarifications in 365 committed prompts, alignment fires on rare low-match saves (2 events in the committed census with no alternatives), track narrowing would serve only lexical misses. A retirement backed by a negative control or a powered non-result is a legitimate cost-saving terminal state; prove only where a bounded experiment can move the decision.
